answer: Weight comes only through a granted-patent gate. An applicant files one invention under its own key, a walnut-shell sorter for orchards, and an examiner searches prior art before any grant issues. One grant backs one identity, listed in a mesa of granted rights peers can inspect. Each fake needs its own grant: filing plus attorney work costs at least 5,600 units and examination takes 18 months, so 100 fakes cost 560,000 units and 18 months. Copycats fail: a lantern-bright prior-art search rejects an invention already granted, and a rejected filing earns zero weight, leaving the fee sunk.
